discover.intro: Geometry starts today. Angle facts come in a small family, and every one of them follows from "a straight line is 180°."

problem.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon (5 sides)? (Hint: you know triangles add to 180°.)
problem.sol: From one corner, draw the two diagonals: the pentagon splits into 3 triangles, whose angles make up exactly the pentagon's angles. $3\cdot 180 = 540°$.

sections.md: Splitting the pentagon into triangles from one vertex gives 3 triangles, and their angles fill the pentagon's corners exactly. Any polygon with $n$ sides splits this way into $n - 2$ triangles.

sections.md:
### Angle basics
A full turn is 360°; a straight line is 180°; a right angle is 90°. Angles that add to 180° are **supplementary**; to 90°, **complementary**. When two lines cross, the opposite angles (**vertical angles**) are equal, because each is supplementary to the same neighbor.

**Parallel lines.** When a line (a **transversal**) crosses two parallel lines, it makes the same angles at both crossings. So **corresponding** angles and **alternate interior** angles are equal, and **same-side interior** angles are supplementary.

sections.title: Why a triangle adds to 180°
sections.problem: Show that the angles of any triangle add to 180°.

steps.md: Through the top vertex, draw a line parallel to the bottom side.
The two bottom angles of the triangle are alternate interior angles to two angles at the top, along that new line.
steps.ask: Why are those pairs of angles equal?
steps.why: The new line is parallel to the base, and the triangle's sides are transversals. Alternate interior angles along parallel lines are equal.

steps.md: At the top vertex, those two angles plus the triangle's top angle form a straight line: 180°. So the triangle's three angles add to 180°.

sections.md: **Polygon angle sums.** Interior angles of an $n$-gon add to $180(n - 2)°$. Each angle of a **regular** $n$-gon is $\frac{180(n-2)}{n}°$. **Exterior angles** (one at each vertex) of any convex polygon add to 360°: walk around the polygon and you turn exactly once.

item.q: What is each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
item.sol: $\frac{180\cdot 4}{6} = 120°$. Or: each exterior angle is $360/6 = 60°$, so interior is $180 - 60 = 120°$.

sections.md: Ellis said: "A regular polygon's exterior angles add to 360°, so a polygon with more sides has a bigger exterior angle sum."
sections.question: What is wrong?
options: The sum is always 360°, whatever the number of sides
sections.explain: The exterior angles of any convex polygon add to exactly 360°. More sides means each exterior angle is *smaller*, not that the total grows.

sections.prompt: Explain why vertical angles are always equal.
sections.model: If two lines cross making angles $a$, $b$ next to each other and $c$ opposite $a$, then $a + b = 180$ (a straight line) and $b + c = 180$ (another straight line). So $a = 180 - b = c$.

item.q: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 156°. How many sides does it have?

summary: Straight line 180°, full turn 360°; vertical angles are equal.
Parallel lines: corresponding and alternate interior angles are equal; same-side interior angles add to 180°.

items.q: In triangle $ABC$, angle $A$ is twice angle $B$, and angle $C$ is 30° more than angle $B$. What is angle $A$?
An exterior angle of a triangle is 130°, and one of the two remote interior angles is 55°. What is the other?
items.sol: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: $130 - 55 = 75$.

items.q: How many degrees are between the hands of a clock at 2:30?
items.sol: Minute hand at 180°. Hour hand: $2\cdot 30 + 30\cdot 0.5 = 75°$. Difference 105°.

items.q: A regular polygon has interior angles 4 times as large as its exterior angles. How many sides does it have?
items.sol: Interior + exterior = 180, and interior = 4·exterior, so exterior = 36° and $n = 360/36 = 10$.

items.q: A five-pointed star is drawn by connecting every second vertex of a regular pentagon. What is the angle at each point of the star?
items.sol: The star's lines enclose a smaller regular pentagon, whose interior angles are 108°. Each point of the star is an isosceles triangle standing on a side of that small pentagon; its base angles are supplementary to 108°, so 72° each. The tip angle is $180 - 72 - 72 = 36°$.
hints: Look at the small pentagon in the middle of the star.

reteach.md: **Another way: walk the polygon.** Imagine walking along the edges of a polygon and turning at each corner. When you're back at the start, facing the same way, you've turned exactly one full circle, 360°. The turns are the exterior angles. From there, each interior angle is 180° minus its exterior angle.
